truth_evidence: Affected 2015.04.28 to 2023.05.07. The vulnerability is a distrusted root CA bundled in the certificate data, not a defect in Python code.

Fix commit 8fb96ed '2023.07.22' removes the e-Tugra root certificates from certifi/cacert.pem; the only other change is the version string. https://github.com/certifi/python-certifi/commit/8fb96ed81f71e7097ed11bc4d9b19afd7ea5c909
The fix commit also bumps __version__ in certifi/__init__.py. That is a module-level change to a .py file and must not be reported as vulnerable code.
No vulnerable function and no entry point exist; reachability is not a meaningful question for this advisory (every TLS verification using certifi.where() uses the bundle).
